title: CIVICUS at the 81st Session of the UN General Assembly
content:
As the United Nations (UN) marks its 81st year, civil society continues to face significant barriers to meaningful participation. During UN General Assembly (UNGA) High-Level Week, these barriers remain visible, from the suspension of badges for ECOSOC-accredited non-governmental organisations (NGOs), to the absence of a permanent platform for civil society engagement, as well as reprisals by States against those who engage with UN processes. These restrictions risk silencing the communities most affected by global crises and undermine the UN’s commitments to inclusivity, participation and accountability. 

This year’s UNGA session is relevant as the UN prepares for a change of leadership from current Secretary General Antonio Gutteres to a new head who will assume office in 2027. In a time of immense geo-political strife, widespread human rights violations, stalling progress on sustainable development and climate catastrophe it is vital that the next UN Secretary General is up to the task and is a woman since the UN has always been headed by a man.
